say: Safety first. Melt over a pot of gently simmering water, called a double boiler. Keep the heat low. Shea should never smoke or boil, and you never leave the pot.

cards.d: Use a double boiler on low heat. Shea should never smoke or boil. Never leave the pot.
Melted oils can cause serious burns. Keep children away from the work area.
Cover the pan with a lid. Never pour water on burning oil.

say: A reliable starting formula is about 70% shea butter and 30% liquid oil. For a 500 g batch, that is 350 g of shea.

panel.heading: Smooth whipped shea, 70% shea
items: Weigh: 70% shea, 30% liquid oil
Melt fully, then hold melted 10 minutes
Cool fast in iced water to soft custard
Add the weighed essential oil when cool
Whip 5 to 10 minutes until fluffy
Fill clean, dry jars and label

say: Slow cooling causes grainy butter. Bisi in Lagos cooled her first batch slowly overnight, and customers said it felt sandy. She remelted, cooled it fast and whipped again, and it was smooth.

panel.rule: Melt fully, hold it melted, then cool fast. That stops grains.

say: Decide what the oil is for before choosing oils. A scalp oil is massaged in a few times a week, so it is light and low in essential oil. Chioma's 100 g scalp oil has 50 g light coconut oil, 29 g olive, 20 g castor, and 1 g lavender.
A sealing oil for lengths and ends can be richer, with castor up to about 40%.
Her label promises softening, not growth.
A balm is oil made solid with wax. About 20% wax gives a firm balm. For 100 g, weigh 20 g beeswax, 30 g shea and 50 g olive oil.

panel.heading: A firm beeswax balm
items: Weigh 20 g beeswax, 30 g shea, 50 g olive oil
Melt on low heat until clear
Spoon test: too hard, add oil; too soft, wax
Add essential oil low; pour and let set

say: Melt over a double boiler on low heat. Beeswax takes longer than shea. Stir until clear.

panel.heading: A firm beeswax balm
items: Weigh 20 g beeswax, 30 g shea, 50 g olive oil
Melt on low heat until clear
Spoon test: too hard, add oil; too soft, wax
Add essential oil low; pour and let set

say: Dip a cold spoon in, let it set for a minute, and press. Too hard, add a little oil. Too soft, add a little wax. Record the change.

say: Stir in essential oil at a low level. On lips, avoid cinnamon, clove and citrus oils. Pour into dry tins and leave to set.

say: The American Academy of Dermatology advises a simple test. Give each tester a labelled sample and the instructions.

panel.heading: Skin test before regular use
items: Give a labelled sample with instructions
Inner arm, twice a day for 7 to 10 days
Redness, itching or swelling: stop and tell you
Clear test: then face, scalp or body

say: Apply the normal amount on the inner arm or elbow bend, twice a day for 7 to 10 days.

say: Test hair products for about four weeks, with at least five testers whose hair is different from yours.
